title: Andhra Pradesh Pours ₹98 Crore Into Suryalanka Beach in Push to Build India's Eastern Goa
excerpt: A Swadesh Darshan 2.0 project, luxury tent cities, beach shacks, and ultra-luxury backwater cruises are transforming Bapatla district's coastline into a major tourism hub.
body:
• A ₹98-crore tourism development project under the Centre's Swadesh Darshan 2.0 scheme is transforming Suryalanka Beach in Bapatla district, Andhra Pradesh, with eco-friendly resorts, food courts, and modern amenities.
  • Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has directed officials to develop 15 km of Suryalanka beachfront and build Maldives-style island tourism, targeting 25,000 hotel rooms statewide by 2028.
  • Beach shack pilot projects at Suryalanka and Visakhapatnam will launch September 1, with luxury tent cities and ultra-luxury backwater boat services also planned for the region.
  • Private firms have pledged ₹12,565 crore in tourism-related investments across Andhra Pradesh since the coalition government took office, expected to generate over 8,000 new hotel rooms.

Andhra Pradesh is channeling ₹98 crore into transforming Suryalanka Beach in Bapatla district into the state's premier coastal tourism destination, with the project now underway as part of the Centre's Swadesh Darshan 2.0 scheme. The development spans more than 20 acres of government land around the beach and includes plans for eco-friendly budget resorts, modern sanitation facilities, food courts, and children's play areas.

The Andhra Pradesh Urban Finance and Infrastructure Development Corporation is overseeing the phased execution, which is designed to attract additional private investment through public-private partnership models. The project also incorporates solid waste management infrastructure, renewable energy systems, and environmental awareness programs aligned with Blue Flag certification standards.

Naidu's Maldives Vision

Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has made Suryalanka the centerpiece of a broader strategy to position Andhra Pradesh as a beach tourism powerhouse. At a State Investment Board meeting, Naidu directed officials to develop the Suryalanka beachfront over a stretch of 15 kilometers as a pollution-free tourism zone.

"We should develop island tourism on the lines of the Maldives. If we can build 25,000 rooms, we can attract tourists."

— N. Chandrababu Naidu, Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh

The vision extends beyond Suryalanka. Naidu wants small islands near Sullurpeta developed alongside the beach, with the Papikondalu-Polavaram region, Konaseema, Pulicat, and Visakhapatnam forming additional tourism clusters. The state tourism corporation has been given a target of generating ₹1,000 crore in revenue over the next 15 years.

Beach Shacks and Tent Cities

The AP government has approved the launch of beach shacks across all 12 coastal districts, with pilot projects at Suryalanka and Visakhapatnam beaches set to open September 1. Visitors will have access to seafood, beverages, beach beds, showers, and other tourist-friendly facilities through 2029.

Separately, a 50-room luxury tent city is planned for Suryalanka through a public-private partnership, modeled after successful tent city operations at Gujarat's Kevadia near the Statue of Unity and at Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh. The initiative is a response to the chronic shortage of quality accommodation in the area — Suryalanka already attracts over one lakh visitors monthly, and nearby Chirala and Ramapuram beaches draw an additional two lakh.

The state is also promoting homestays, with over 1,800 old village houses identified for renovation to offer tourists an authentic rural experience.

Luxury Backwater Cruises

The Andhra Pradesh Tourism Development Corporation has granted approval for five ultra-luxury tourist boats to operate in the backwaters near Suryalanka. Three vessels, offering two- to four-bedroom configurations, will cruise up to 30 kilometers through scenic backwaters from Nagarjuna Canal to Nizampatnam. The luxury boats are expected to be operational by October 2026, drawing inspiration from Kerala's popular houseboat tourism model.

What It Means for Diaspora Travelers

For NRIs from Andhra Pradesh, the developments offer a significant upgrade to a coastline long overshadowed by Goa and Kerala in India's tourism landscape. The state recorded 309.2 million tourist visits last year, with a 21 percent growth rate in the first nine months of the current year. Private firms have pledged ₹12,565 crore in tourism-related investments since the coalition government took office, expected to generate 8,073 new rooms across hotels and resorts.

Looking Ahead

The state plans seaplane services under the UDAN scheme, water aerodromes at Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada, Srisailam, and Gandikota, and cruise tourism from Visakhapatnam and Krishnapatnam Port. The larger aim is to position Andhra Pradesh's 1,000-kilometer coastline as a serious alternative to India's established beach tourism destinations under the Swarnandhra 2047 vision.
